source_text:
Εἰ δὲ ταῦτα ἴδια μέν ἐστιν ψυχῆς, ἐκ περιουσίας δὲ τὰς κρείττους ἐπιδέχονται προσθήκας, ἆρ' οὖν ὅτι συναυξάνει μὲν τῷ σώματι, καθάπερ δὲ τοῦτο λεληθότως ὑπαναλέγεται τὰς δυνάμεις, οὕτω καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ προκόπτουσα τὸν νοῦν· ὅσοι δὲ μηδέποτε βαίνουσιν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄμεινον, ἀλλὰ μωροὶ διαμένουσιν, δῆλον ὅτι
λελωβημένου τινὸς μορίου ἀτελεῖς ἔχουσι τὰς ψυχὰς, ὥσπερ οἱ τὴν φρενίτιδα ἀρρωστήσαντες νόσον. Ἀμέλει καὶ τὸ τοῦ πρωτοπλάστου σῶμα σχηματισθὲν ἔκειτο νεκρὸν, ἄπνουν, ἀκίνητον μέλεσιν μὲν καὶ ἁρμονίᾳ ῥερυθμισμένον ἄκρως, μορφῇ τε καὶ κάλλει κεκοσμημένον ἐμπρεπῶς ἅτε δὴ καὶ παρ' αὐτοῦ πλάστου γεννηθὲν τοῦ Θεοῦ πρωτότυπον ἄγαλμα καὶ τῆς θεσπεσιωτάτης εἰκόνος ἐκτυπωθὲν ἀφομοίωμα κράτιστον, ἀναίσθητον δὲ καὶ ἄφωνον καὶ ἄπνουν· ὡς δὲ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ δημιουργικῶς ἐνεφύσησεν ὁ Θεὸς, αὐτίκα τὴν κίνησιν εἴληφεν· ἐξ ἐκείνου δὲ βαδίζει καὶ ἀναπνεῖ καὶ φθέγγεται, ἄρχει λογίζεται πράττει διοικεῖ. 6 Κοινὸν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς πάθος ὕπνος.
thought_title: Soul grows with body; first-formed body lifeless until God breathed
orientation: Eustathius is concluding his argument against the philosophers by showing that the soul's powers develop with the body, and that even the first-formed human body lay lifeless until God breathed into it.
pass_a_gloss: But if these things are proper to the soul, and from abundance they admit the better additions, then is it not the case that it grows together with the body, and just as this body gradually develops its powers, so also the soul as it advances gathers up the mind? But as many as never go on to the better, but remain foolish, it is clear that because some part has been damaged they have incomplete souls, just as those who have fallen ill with the disease of madness. Certainly also the body of the first-formed human, having been shaped, lay dead, breathless, motionless, in limbs and harmony arranged to the highest degree, in form and beauty adorned fittingly, inasmuch as it was born from the Creator God himself as a first-model statue and a most excellent copy impressed from the most divine image, but unfeeling and voiceless and breathless. But when God breathed into his face in the manner of a craftsman, immediately it received movement. And from that time it walks and breathes and speaks, rules, reasons, acts, administers. Sleep is a condition common to body and soul.

choices.why: Renders the idiomatic phrase literally, preserving the sense of having more than enough, without smoothing into 'abundantly' or 'as a surplus'.
The verb combines 'under' and 'gather up'; 'secretly' captures the hidden, gradual acquisition of powers, matching the contrast with the soul's progress.

choices.english: because some part has been damaged
choices.why: Keeps the genitive absolute causal force and the indefinite 'some part', preserving the medical analogy of bodily damage causing incomplete souls.
Renders both words literally: 'first-model' for the unique original pattern, 'statue' for the crafted image, avoiding interpretive 'archetype' or 'image'.

choices.english: in the manner of a craftsman
choices.why: Adverbial form of 'demiurge/craftsman'; the literal rendering preserves the artisan metaphor Eustathius applies to God's breathing.
Keeps the asyndetic sequence of four finite verbs in the same order, preserving the rapid list of activities that follow the breathing.
rejected: it rules and reasons and acts and administers

pass_b_english: But if these powers belong to the soul itself, and it receives its better additions superabundantly, then surely the soul grows together with the body. Just as the body gradually develops its powers, so too the soul advances in mind. And those who never step toward what is better but remain foolish clearly have incomplete souls because some part has been damaged, just like those who have fallen ill with the disease of madness. Certainly the body of the first-formed human also lay dead after it was shaped—breathless, motionless, yet arranged to the highest degree in its limbs and joints, and fittingly adorned in form and beauty, since it was created by the Creator God himself as a first-model statue and impressed as the finest copy from the most divine image. But it was without sensation, without speech, and without breath. Then, when God breathed into its face in the manner of a craftsman, it immediately received movement. From that moment it walks and breathes and speaks; it rules, reasons, acts, administers. In this way, sleep is a condition common to body and soul.

problems.why: ἐκ περιουσίας means 'in abundance' or 'superabundantly,' not 'from abundance' as a source.
problems.fix: and receives its better additions superabundantly

problems.quote: then does the soul not grow together with the body?
problems.source_quote: ἆρ' οὖν ὅτι συναυξάνει μὲν τῷ σώματι
problems.why: Source is a confident statement 'surely then it grows together with the body,' not a negative question.
problems.fix: then surely it grows together with the body

problems.why: ὑπαναλέγεται means 'uses up' or 'consumes,' not 'gathers up'; the body secretly depletes its powers.
problems.fix: just as the body secretly uses up its powers
problems.ruling: ὑπαναλέγεται means 'consumes/uses up,' not 'gathers up'; body depletes powers, changing meaning.

problems.why: γεννηθέν here means 'created/made,' not 'born from'; the body was fashioned by God, not born from him.
problems.fix: since it was created by the Creator God himself
problems.ruling: γεννηθὲν here means 'made/created' by God the πλάστης, not 'born from,' misleading re creation.

problems.quote: in the manner of a craftsman
problems.why: δημιουργικῶς means 'creatively' or 'as Creator,' referring to God's creative power, not human craftsmanship; 'craftsman' diminishes the divine act.
problems.fix: when God breathed creatively into its face
problems.ruling: δημιουργικῶς means 'as Creator/creatively'; 'manner of a craftsman' misleads re divine creative act.

edits.old: and it receives its better additions from abundance
edits.new: and it receives its better additions superabundantly

edits.old: then does the soul not grow together with the body?
edits.new: then surely it grows together with the body

edits.old: Just as the body secretly gathers up its powers
edits.new: Just as the body secretly uses up its powers

edits.old: since it was born from the Creator God himself
edits.new: since it was created by the Creator God himself

edits.old: when God breathed into its face in the manner of a craftsman
edits.new: when God breathed creatively into its face

problems.quote: stamped out as the finest copy
problems.fix: Clarify if model or copy is meant

problems.quote: then surely it grows together with the body Just as
problems.why: Missing period and sentence break; two sentences run together.
problems.fix: Insert period: '…with the body. Just as…'

problems.quote: it receives its better additions superabundantly
problems.why: 'It' is ambiguous—could refer to soul or body; antecedent is unclear across the sentence break.
'Frenzy' is an archaic rendering; context suggests a specific mental or neurological illness.

problems.quote: Sleep is a condition common to body and soul.
problems.why: Appears abruptly with no connection to preceding argument; reader cannot tell if it is a new thesis or a conclusion.
problems.fix: Add a transitional clause linking sleep to the body-soul discussion.

edits.old: then surely it grows together with the body Just as
edits.new: then surely the soul grows together with the body. Just as

edits.old: and stamped out as the finest copy of the most divine image
edits.new: and stamped out as the finest copy from the most divine image

edits.old: Sleep is a condition common to body and soul.
edits.new: In this way, sleep is a condition common to body and soul.

fixed: The English 'it receives its better additions superabundantly' was flagged for ambiguous 'it', but the edit to 'the soul' is included in the sentence-break fix.
The 'first-model statue' and 'copy' contradiction is resolved by using 'archetypal statue' and clarifying 'copy from the most divine image'.

problems.quote: the body secretly uses up its powers
problems.why: 'Secretly uses up' is opaque; contradicts visible aging
Platonic term oddly applied to Adam's body before ensoulment; may mislead
problems.fix: Verify if 'archetypal' or 'archetype-worthy' intended; add note

problems.quote: stamped out as the finest copy from the most divine image
problems.why: Mixed metaphor: 'stamped out' suggests coining, 'copy from image' suggests painting
problems.fix: Check Greek for single coherent image; 'impressed as' or 'minted as'

problems.quote: when God breathed creatively into its face
problems.why: Alludes to Genesis 2:7 but 'creatively' is interpretive addition not in biblical text
problems.fix: Note this is theological paraphrase, not direct quotation

problems.quote: the body secretly uses up its powers
problems.why: 'Uses up' implies depletion, but context argues the body develops its powers gradually.

edits.old: Just as the body secretly uses up its powers, so too the soul advances in mind.
edits.new: Just as the body gradually develops its powers, so too the soul advances in mind.

edits.old: and stamped out as the finest copy from the most divine image
edits.new: and impressed as the finest copy from the most divine image

edits.old: when God breathed creatively into its face
edits.new: when God breathed into its face in the manner of a craftsman

fixed: The body's powers: changed 'secretly uses up' to 'gradually develops' to match the source's sense of growth, not depletion.
Archetypal statue: changed to 'first-model statue' to avoid misleading Platonic overtones while preserving the Greek πρωτότυπον.
Stamped out: changed to 'impressed' to avoid the coining metaphor and better match the image-copy language.
Breathed creatively: restored 'in the manner of a craftsman' to remove the interpretive addition and stay closer to the source.

last_rejected.quote: then surely it grows together with the body Just as
last_rejected.source_quote: ἆρ' οὖν ὅτι συναυξάνει μὲν τῷ σώματι, καθάπερ δὲ
last_rejected.why: Sentence break lost; 'ἆρ' οὖν ὅτι' introduces the conclusion. Missing punctuation makes it unreadable.
last_rejected.fix: then surely it grows together with the body. Just as
last_rejected.ruling: Missing comma/semicolon after 'body' is minor punctuation, not meaning change; 'ἆρ' οὖν ὅτι' force is still conveyed by 'then surely'.

last_rejected.why: πρωτότυπον means 'original' or 'archetype', not 'first-model'; ἄγαλμα is 'statue/image'.
last_rejected.ruling: πρωτότυπον can mean 'first-model/original'; ἄγαλma as 'statue' is valid. Meaning preserved.

last_rejected.quote: stamped out as the finest copy
last_rejected.why: ἐκτυπωθὲν means 'formed/molded', not 'stamped out'; ἀφομοίωμα is 'likeness', not 'copy'.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκτυπωθὲν includes 'stamped/molded'; ἀφομοίωμα as 'copy/likeness' is within range.

last_rejected.why: φρενῖτις is 'phrenitis', inflammation of the brain/delirium, not 'frenzy' (μανία).
last_rejected.ruling: φρενῖτις denotes delirious frenzy; 'frenzy' is acceptable rendering, not a major error.
